boardRows.decisionBasis: AJ Dybantsa is the clear top choice based on team needs (alpha scorer, wing creator, defensive size) and priority tags (wing creator, star upside, two-way). Tool analysis ranks him highest (finalScore 90.72), with elite creation (94) and upside (98). Team preference entry selects him with confidence 96 and overlap families (wing, creation, defense, upside_asset). RAG snippets consistently project him at #1 for Washington. Alternative Darryn Peterson lacks wing size/creation fit despite higher consensus rank. Evidence is strong from multiple locked artifacts and normalized data; no risks or conflicting signals undermine this selection.

Utah Jazz holds explicit guard/creation/shooting need with frontcourt fit concerns. Darryn Peterson is the cleanest fit as the top-ranked consensus guard, offering primary initiator skills, pull-up shooting, and high-usage creation. Multiple locked artifacts and project reports align on this selection with a margin of 3-5. Needs are strongly matched: primary guard, shot creation, late-clock offense. Risk tolerance 78 favors high-upside lead guard.

Memphis needs a frontcourt engine with rebounding and feel; Cameron Boozer is the highest-rated shortlist candidate who fits exactly, matching priority tags and team preference. Multiple mock drafts and the core board project Boozer to Memphis at pick 3 with high confidence.

Caleb Wilson is the consensus #4 prospect, a big wing/forward who perfectly matches Chicago Bulls' explicit needs for size, defense, rim pressure, and two-way play. He is the top-ranked frontcourt player remaining on the board after the first three picks, and all tool results (clean RAG, candidate analysis, team preference model) strongly support this selection. No alternative from the shortlist offers a comparable combination of fit, consensus, and two-way upside.

Keaton Wagler is the consensus 5th pick, matches Clippers' need for a big guard/shooter with pull-up shooting and decision-making, supported by tool analysis (score 86.5) and cleanRag snippet confirming pick 5 in core board and team fit discussion. The team preference model also strongly selects Wagler with confidence 89.
Based on toolShortlist analysis showing Acuff as top fit for primary guard needs, supported by core board projection and team preference model despite mixed intel signals.
明确团队需求为控球后卫深度/节奏/防守活性；优先级标签为主要后卫/节奏/组织；候选人与偏好直接匹配（primary guard, pull-up shooting, decision maker, pace）；模拟董事会和偏好报告一致指向Mikel Brown Jr.；分差极窄但偏好口径支持该选择。

Atlanta's needs are rim protection, frontcourt size, and vertical spacing. Aday Mara is the top available center with rare height (7-3), shot-blocking, and interior finishing. Multiple project reports and team preference signals point to Mara as the best fit. Guard-heavy board already depleted; this pick addresses clear need. Despite mixed signal confidence from team preference engine, Mara is the most prudent selection from the shortlist.

Selected from toolShortlist. Team needs two-way guard, shooting, secondary creation. Burries fits priority tags combo guard, shooter, two-way. Overlap families [guard, shooting, defense] perfectly match team requirements. Consensus rank 11 and strong RAG evidence from project reports (prediction_strategy_audit, main_parameter_board_simulation) projecting Burries at pick 9. Kingston Flemings considered but better suited as primary guard (rank 8, higher creation less shooting), and Cameron Carr (rank 21) less consensus support.

Multiple high-trust sources (ESPN, The Athletic, locked artifact board) converge on Flemings as the optimal pick for Milwaukee. He fits the Bucks' prioritized guard/creation/defense tags, provides immediate point-of-attack defense and playmaking, and aligns with the team's contend-phase need for a connector guard who can play off Giannis. Analytical scoring also supports him as the top shortlist candidate (finalScore 83.8).

Highest finalScore (77.561) in toolShortlist, alignment with team's shooting need and weak preference for Nate Ament as shooter/stretch forward, supported by multiple mock drafts (core-board pick 11). Nate Ament's strengths include floor spacing and size, fitting the Warriors' system that rewards processing and low-mistake play. Weak preference for guard is overridden by higher score and consensus.

boardRows.decisionBasis: Highest tool shortlist score (84.7) with perfect overlap of team need families (wing, frontcourt, defense, feel). Team preference entry selects Lendeborg with high confidence. Multiple cleanRAG snippets predict this player at pick 12. Consensus rank matches pick; role tags (connector, rebounder, defense, maturity, feel) align with team's priority of versatile forward with defensive and feel attributes.

Karim Lopez is the top-ranked candidate in the tool analysis with a final score of 81.5, driven by strong consensus (consensus rank 14, international upside) and high need alignment (overlap families: wing, frontcourt, defense). His profile as a 6-8 big wing with defensive tools, athleticism, and transition offense matches Miami's explicit need for a physical wing with two-way toughness and self-creation potential. RAG evidence confirms him as the predicted pick in the core board with confidence 88 and margin 3. Other frontcourt options lack the combo of wing skills, creation, and upside.

Team has explicit need for frontcourt defense, rebounding, and finishing. Morez Johnson Jr. is the highest-scoring candidate in the tool shortlist (finalScore 79.83), and his role tags (rebounder, rim protector, finisher, size) align perfectly with team needs. RAG evidence confirms Charlotte should use one of their two first-round picks on a frontcourt player. Team preference entry selects Morez and fits all priority tags.

Chicago targets frontcourt depth, shooting, and upside at pick 15. Allen Graves profiles as a stretch forward with defense, rebounding, and forward size, directly matching the team's explicit needs. He complements the prior pick (Caleb Wilson, SF/PF) and satisfies the team's priority tags (stretch forward, rebounder, size, defense). Supported by tool analysis and team preference entry.

Team needs rim protection and size; Chris Cenac Jr. is the highest-scoring frontcourt prospect in the shortlist with rim protector role, strong defensive profile, and upside. He fits the need better than Hannes Steinbach despite team preference selection, offering superior defense and athleticism.

Thunder asset phase tolerates upside development; team priority big wing, shooting, stash optionality. Dailyn Swain (SF/PF) directly addresses big wing need with size (6-7, 211 lbs), defensive activity (83), feel (82), and upside (80). Overlaps team priority families (wing, frontcourt, upside). Non‑international, but stash optionality is secondary. Previous pick Lendeborg (12) is also SF/PF, but Swain adds defensive versatility and passing, complementing roster. Shortlist guards (Anderson, Philon, Carr) lack big wing size; international frontcourt Steinbach lacks primary wing label.

boardRows.decisionBasis: Toronto's explicit needs for length, team defense, and a connector forward align with Steinbach's profile as a 6-10 connector with high feel and rebounding. His frontcourt fit and low-mistake style fit the accelerate phase. Labaron Philon Jr. has higher consensus but lacks the defensive size and length the Raptors prioritize.

Team need for shooting/secondary handler/spacing; priority tags combo guard/shooter/decision maker; tool analysis and RAG data (main parameter board, prediction audit) both align on Stirtz as the best fit at 20 for San Antonio. Margin is narrow, but Stirtz's mature decision-making, shooting (84), and feel (88) complement the Spurs' frontcourt creation.

Pistons need wing shooting, defensive activity, floor spacing; toolShortlist top fit is Cameron Carr with highest score 84.257 and strong need/family overlap (guard, wing, shooting, defense). cleanRag snippets repeatedly project Carr to Pistons at pick 21. TeamPreferenceEntry also matches with high confidence. No reason to deviate.

Team need fit prioritized shooting, size, and defense. Isaiah Evans (6-6 wing shooter, 86 shooting, 76 defense) aligns better with priorityTags (shooter, size, defense) than top-scored Labaron Philon Jr. (6-3 guard). CleanRAG snippets indicate Philadelphia’s pick 22 preference shifts to Evans when both are available, favoring his 3-and-D profile over Philon’s creation. Dailyn Swain (earlier preference) was off the board at pick 17.

Philon is the top-scoring candidate on the toolShortlist (74.179). His role tags ('primary guard', 'pace', 'shot creator', 'playmaking') strongly align with Atlanta's priority tags ('primary guard', 'defense', 'pace'). His strengths in fast decision-making and scoring/passing balance address the playmaking need better than Okorie, who is primarily a scoring guard with noted playmaking-balance risks. Philadelphia's prior pick of Mara at center confirms the backcourt need at 23. Audit signals suggesting a shift from Okorie to Philon further support this selection.

RAG team-preference snippet explicitly names Koa Peat for pick 24, stating 'Koa Peat, a mature guard, or backup-center profile should be favored over raw upside.' Prediction strategy audit also selects Peat. Team fits toughness and frontcourt needs; shooting is below ideal but maturity and defensive role outweigh.

Lakers need wing shooting/size/low-usage defense; preferred wings Dailyn Swain and Isaiah Evans already picked. Among available shortlist, Henri Veesaar is the highest‑scoring frontcourt option (71.9) with strong defensive profile (81 defense, 94 size) and clean RAG reference as a projected pick. His low‑usage rim protection and finishing fit the size/frontcourt priority. No true 3‑and‑D big wing on shortlist; Veesaar is the safest frontcourt upgrade.

Tobe Awaka aligns closely with Denver's priority tags (connector, rebounder, feel) and offers frontcourt depth as a big wing who can defend, pass, and complement Jokic in a motion offense. ToolShortlist shows overlapping needs and his profile (defense 73.3, feel 72, size 82.6) fits despite lower consensus rank. Selected over Tarris Reed Jr. due to superior feel and connector traits, and over Jayden Quaintance due to medical risk and lower feel score.

Boston's priority tags are two-way, big wing, shooter. Tyler Bilodeau, a 6-8 senior from UCLA, fits as a big wing with shooting (65), defensive versatility (72.2), and the ability to defend multiple spots, directly addressing the roster note. His need fit score (84) is the highest in the shortlist, outweighing his lower consensus rank.

Meleek Thomas is the highest-scoring shortlist guard with strong combo guard creation, shooting, and bench scoring, directly matching Minnesota’s explicit needs for guard creation and point-of-attack defense. Clean RAG confirms team fit at pick 28. Other guards lack clean consensus or fit signals; frontcourt options do not address the priority combo‑guard need.

Team needs center depth and size. ESPN mock and cleanRag snippet both signal Tarris Reed Jr. as a fit for Cleveland at 29. Higher floor as a senior center aligns with contending phase and moderate risk tolerance.
